Coupled sparse log-concave factorization of multiple samples

Source: R/coupledNMF.R
coupledNMF.Rd

Align related multichannel samples and estimate common spectra with sample-specific nonnegative areas, log-concave profiles and backgrounds. Observations remain on their original time grids. Samples are read from a disk-backed store one at a time during fitting.

Usage

coupledNMF(
  samples,
  family = poisson("identity"),
  lambda = "gic",
  path = tempfile("coupledNMF_"),
  precluster = 32L,
  dispersion = NULL,
  theta = NULL,
  method = c("cosine", "hellinger"),
  align = TRUE,
  ncores = NULL,
  control = list(),
  verbose = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
fitted(object, sample = 1L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
coef(object, sample = NULL, normalize = c("none", "l1"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
AIC(object, ..., k = 2)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
BIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
GIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
EBIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
MBIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coupledNMF'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("areas", "spectra", "profiles"),
  sample = NULL,
  compounds = seq_len(min(6L, nrow(x$P))),
  ...
)

Arguments

samples

List of sample descriptions. Each contains y (a numeric scans-by-channels matrix, or an RDS file containing one), increasing time, and optionally X, background, fit, weights, offset, exposure, sample_id, group, small_width and edges. Large weights and offset matrices can also be supplied as RDS paths. fit is a splogconNMF() initializer or its RDS path. Without a fit, X supplies candidate profiles; otherwise estimate_psf() estimates them. Channel names and ordering must agree across samples. Times and small_width use the same units. Shared scan-wise weights and offsets remain vectors throughout coupled fitting; each mass channel reuses the same values.

family

Identity-link signal family supported by splogconNMF(): Gaussian, Poisson, quasipoisson, NB2, NB1, censored Gamma or common-scale Gamma.

lambda

Information-criterion preset or nonnegative penalty per selection degree of freedom. The selection count is (channels - 1) * shared_compounds + detected_occurrences, plus estimated noise parameters. Background and profile complexity are unpenalized.

path

New directory for the sample store and fitted factors. Keep this directory with the saved R object; its paths are used by fitted() and plots.

precluster

Maximum outcome groups for independent initialization. Coupled refinement and selection always use all original channels.

dispersion, theta

Shared-across-channels noise parameters, as in splogconNMF(). They may be supplied per sample in its description. Resolved dispersions are frozen; a negative NB2 theta enables bounded likelihood-improving shape updates in the coupled iterations.

method

Spectral distance for anchor matching and grouping.

align

Estimate monotone sample-level time warps.

ncores

Number of native OpenMP threads; defaults to physical cores.

control

Named controls: cycles=10L, initial_cycles=5L, rounds=3L, q=64L, rt_tolerance=NULL, alignment_window=NULL, ridge=TRUE, censor=0.5, correlation="none", and initial=list() for controls passed to independent splogconNMF() fits. Default matching windows are derived from the supplied or estimated narrow-peak widths.

verbose

Print initialization and coupled objective progress.

object, x

A fitted coupled model.

sample

One sample index or name; NULL in coef() returns consensus spectra, and in plot() selects all samples.

...

Additional method arguments.

normalize

Return unit-sum spectra or amplitude-scaled spectra.

k

Information-criterion multiplier for AIC().

type

Plot sample areas, common spectra or aligned compound profiles.

compounds

Compound indices to display.

Value

A coupledNMF object with consensus spectra P, integrated areas, occurrence table compounds, monotone alignment, disk-backed factor paths and sample store, objective history, likelihood and timings. fitted(object, sample=...) reconstructs one sample on its original grid.

Details

Let u = w_s(t) be a monotone alignment map and J its binwise Jacobian. With supplied exposure e, the original-grid mean is $$\mu_{sij}=e_{si}\{J_{si}\sum_g a_{sg}h_{sg}(u_{si})p_{gj} +(B_s A_s)_{ij}\}+o_{sij}.$$ Spectra satisfy \(\sum_j p_{gj}=1\); profiles satisfy \(\sum_i\Delta u_{si}h_{sg}(u_{si})=1\) and have concave logarithms in actual aligned time. Thus areas integrate the fitted rate over original time. exposure=1 models the supplied intensities. For integrated counts, known integration durations can instead be supplied as exposure. Scan spacing, per-mass dwell time and vendor abundance units are distinct quantities. No exposure is inferred from the number of nonzero mass traces.

Reciprocal spectral matches supply leading-edge anchors: the 1%-height start plus half the local narrow-peak width. A robust low-dimensional drift spline includes log area ratio as a nuisance covariate; only drift enters the warp. Positive-slope projection gives a monotone map. Grouping pools compatible spectra algebraically, with at most one occurrence per sample and an area-ordered profile-overlap check. It performs no model refits. Subsequent local profile, pooled spectral and background updates are backtracked against the full original-channel likelihood. A grouped proposal is retained only when the complete penalized objective improves.

The grouping criterion counts shared spectral parameters and detected sample-specific amplitudes; hard shape constraints control profile geometry. It is a rank-selection criterion with unpenalized profile and baseline complexity. Quasipoisson uses the scaled likelihood kernel described in splogconNMF(). Noise scales are held fixed when comparing groupings. Undetected sample-compound combinations have NA area and are not filled in.

See also

splogconNMF(), estimate_psf(), simulate_GCMS_samples()

Examples

set.seed(19)
n <- 100L; m <- 6L
X <- convmatrix(dnorm(-6:6, sd=1.5), n)
H <- X[, c(25, 65)]; H <- H %*% Matrix::Diagonal(x=1/colSums(H))
S <- matrix(rexp(2*m, 1/2000), 2, m)
samples <- lapply(1:3, function(s) list(
  y=matrix(rpois(n*m, as.matrix(H %*% (S*s))+1), n, m),
  time=seq_len(n), X=X, background=matrix(1,n,1), small_width=9))
fit <- coupledNMF(samples, ncores=1L,
  control=list(cycles=2L, initial_cycles=1L, rounds=1L,
    initial=list(profile_cycles=0L, original_cleanup=FALSE)))
fit$areas
GIC(fit)
